name: Continue with Atmosphere
summary: The one door into signing in and creating an account, in every app. It looks the same everywhere, so people learn it once.

when: On an app's sign-in screen, as the way to sign in with an Atmosphere account.
As the way to create an account too: Front Door asks which once it opens.

whenNot.text: For anything other than opening Front Door.
Restyled to match the app. Its look is the point.

anatomy.description: A pill with a strong border, in the Atmosphere colours.
Decorative: the label names the button.
“Continue with Atmosphere”, from the catalogue, in the person's language.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fills the width of its container, as on a narrow sign-in screen.

states.name: Hover
states.description: The surface changes to its hover colour.

states.name: Focus
states.description: A 2px focus ring, 2px away from the pill.

states.name: Long label
states.description: In long languages, the label wraps onto two lines instead of overflowing.

events.name: click
events.when: It's pressed. The app opens Front Door.

accessibility.name: “Continue with Atmosphere”, in the page's language. The mark is hidden from screen readers.
notes: Its target is 56px high, larger than the 44px minimum (WCAG 2.5.5).
Its label is locked copy: apps can't change it.

guidelines: The label is always “Continue with Atmosphere”: it works for signing in and for creating an account.

terms.meaning: One account that works across every Atmosphere app, hosted by a provider such as Bluesky.

dosAndDonts.do: Use it as it is, in every app.
dosAndDonts.dont: Change its colours, shape or label to match the app.

dosAndDonts.do: Use it for both signing in and creating an account.
dosAndDonts.dont: Add a separate “Create an Atmosphere account” button.

evidence.point: A single, recognisable button lowers the effort of choosing how to sign in, as “Sign in with Apple” and “Sign in with Google” do.
One door for both journeys: Front Door checks for an existing account before creating a new one, so people don't make duplicates.
